### DuplicatePeerId

A [ TrustStore](https://docs.rs/struct.TrustStore.html) insert was rejected because the

[already resolves to a different entry. Duplicate](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/comms/struct.PeerId.html)

`PeerId`[is legal; a duplicate](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/comms/struct.PeerName.html)

`PeerName`[is structurally impossible by design.](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/comms/struct.PeerId.html)

`PeerId`[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ZeroPubkey)

### ZeroPubkey

A trust entry carried the all-zero public key sentinel instead of real Ed25519 key material.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.PeerIdPubkeyMismatch)

### PeerIdPubkeyMismatch

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidPeerName)

### InvalidPeerName

A persisted or wire trust row carried a display name that fails
[ PeerName](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/comms/struct.PeerName.html) validation. The row is rejected fail-closed rather than
coerced into a sanitized name.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidPeerAddress)

### InvalidPeerAddress

A persisted or wire trust row carried an address that fails
[ PeerAddress](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/comms/struct.PeerAddress.html) validation. The row is rejected fail-closed rather
than reinterpreted as a default transport.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ConflictingGeneratedTrustSource)

### ConflictingGeneratedTrustSource

A generated authority source tried to re-add a peer row with different routing material. Callers must use the owning generated rebind/update protocol instead of letting a trust repair rewrite the row.

pub enum TrustResolveError {

```
[PeerName](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/comms/struct.PeerName.html)),
    Ambiguous {
        name: [PeerName](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/comms/struct.PeerName.html),
        candidates: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[PeerId](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/comms/struct.PeerId.html)>,

Error resolving a [ PeerName](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/comms/struct.PeerName.html) to a routing-key

[.](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/comms/struct.PeerId.html)

`PeerId`Two entries may legitimately share a name; the resolver refuses to guess.
Callers that receive `Ambiguous` must disambiguate by other means (ask the

never collapses ambiguous names onto a single routing key.

# TrustStore in meerkat_comms::trust - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/meerkat-comms/0.7.12/meerkat_comms/trust/struct.TrustStore.html

`pub struct TrustStore { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Trust store keyed by canonical [ PeerId](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/comms/struct.PeerId.html).

`PeerName` is **not** a routing key. Duplicate `PeerName` across entries is
legal — duplicate `PeerId` is a hard error. Reverse lookups by name go
through [ resolve_name](https://docs.rs/struct.TrustStore.html#method.resolve_name) which returns a typed
ambiguity error when the name maps to more than one entry.

This type is THE owner of comms trust state: the router’s live trust
projection, ingress classification/admission, and the durable
`trusted_peers.json` projection all key on it. Mutation of live trust
flows exclusively through the generated
`CommsRuntime::apply_trust_mutation` seam.

or

`TrustResolveError::Ambiguous`**not**pick one for you — duplicate names are a discovery concern, not a routing concern.

`pub struct TrustedPeersView { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Read-only handle to the router-owned live trust projection.

The lock itself is not exposed publicly because trust changes affect
admission and routing semantics. Mutation is restricted to the generated
`CommsRuntime::apply_trust_mutation` path.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/meerkat_comms/types.rs.html#157-200)#### pub fn [signable_bytes](https://docs.rs#method.signable_bytes)(&self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/meerkat_comms/types.rs.html#157-200)

#### pub fn [signable_bytes](https://docs.rs#method.signable_bytes)(&self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Compute canonical CBOR bytes to sign: `[id, from, to, kind]`.

Field order is fixed per spec for cross-implementation compatibility.

Note: `ciborium`’s serde `into_writer` does **not** sort map keys. To ensure
deterministic (RFC 8949) encoding, we serialize into `ciborium::value::Value`,
then recursively sort all maps by canonical key order before encoding.

`PubKey` is encoded as a CBOR byte string (major type 2), not an array.
